prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a top-down view where the seated camera wearer looks down at their own arms, hands, and lap (brightest, 0.3–0.6 m away) facing a second seated person across from them whose lower legs and bare feet with toe separators rest on a raised pedicure footrest box (mid-grey, 0.7–1.0 m away) about 0.3–0.5 m beyond the wearer's hands, above a dark tiled floor (1.1–1.4 m below the camera). Across frames 1 to 3, the camera wearer lifts an oval blue basin from above the footrest (around 0.6 m away, partially occluding the footrest and the other person's right foot in frame 1) and sets it down to the right on the floor (receding into darker grey at 1.1–1.3 m in frames 3–4), before lifting a white towel from their lap closer to the camera (0.4–0.5 m) in frames 4–5 while a tall supply cart enters on the far left at 0.5–0.7 m. Both the footrest, the basin, the towel, the cart, and the other person's feet remain within arm's reach of the camera wearer, while the other person's upper body and head are completely out of view above the top edge so whether they look toward the wearer cannot be seen directly, though their feet point toward the wearer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the elevated footrest and left-side supply cart from the recessed floor and tracks the basin's downward trajectory from lap height to floor level. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 3 where the other person's upper-left legs and the footrest box are over-brightened to appear closer than the wearer's hands, and in frame 4 where the black cushion on the footrest is rendered as a smooth convex bulge rather than a flat surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground regions in the pedicure workspace, showing the camera wearer's extended arms at the bottom (0.3–0.6 m from the camera), the oval basin in the center-to-right region (moving from 0.6 m down to 1.2 m on the floor across frames 1–3), and the second person's lower legs and feet at the top-left (0.7–1.0 m away, facing toward the camera wearer with their upper body out of frame). Across frames 1 to 3, the basin mask shifts rightward and shrinks as it is lowered from above the footrest to the floor on the right, removing the occlusion over the footrest, while in frames 4 and 5 a single large mask covers the wearer's arms, lap towel, and the other person's feet at the center and bottom. The basin, towel, and the other person's feet are all within arm's reach of the camera wearer (within 0.8 m), spaced 0.2–0.5 m apart from one another. While the masks highlight the sharp silhouette and rightward displacement of the oval basin and foreground limbs against the unsegmented floor, the map is highly unreliable in both semantics and instance separation. It misclassifies the blue pedicure basin as a 'frisbee' in frames 1–2 and a 'person' in frame 3, splits the camera wearer's left and right arms and the other person's legs into separate 'person' instances in frames 2–3, merges the wearer's arms, white towel, footrest cushion, and the other person's feet into a single 'person' mask in frames 4–5, and completely misses the footrest box, nail polish rack, and left-side tool cart.
descriptions.pose: The pose map plots 2D body skeletons (yellow) and hand keypoints (magenta) in the camera wearer's immediate workspace (0.3–0.8 m away), capturing the wearer's left and right hands gripping the rims of the basin in frames 1 and 2 as it moves rightward, only the wearer's right hand on the basin rim in frame 3, and both hands raised closer to the camera (0.4–0.5 m) holding the white towel in frames 4 and 5. In frames 4 and 5, it allows tracking the inward convergence of the wearer's hands (from ~0.4 m apart on the basin to ~0.15 m apart bunching the towel) and shows the elbows flexing outward on either side of the lap within arm's reach of the other person's feet just above them (0.7–1.0 m away). It makes the fine finger flexion and grip orientation of the wearer's hands explicit even when partially occluded by the basin rim or white towel folds in the RGB image. However, the pose map is severely unreliable for overall scene layout and multi-person understanding because it completely fails to detect the camera wearer's left hand in frame 3 and misses the second person's legs and feet in frames 2–5. Furthermore, because the egocentric top-down viewpoint truncates both people's heads and torsos, the pose estimator hallucinates tiny, inverted full-body torso-and-head skeletons onto the other person's feet and footrest in frame 1 and onto the camera wearer's lap towel and arms in frames 4 and 5, providing false body orientation cues.
